scope: CH-04F Node owned-child model control and trusted credential consumption

evidence.note: Expected public control methods and trusted store consumption did not exist.

Two valid product failures: ready followed by a malformed frame could publish startup success, and BOM was stripped before canonical validation. The third failure was a synthetic fixture error: stdout.end did not close the Windows OS pipe while that fixture stayed alive; it was corrected to flush and exit.
Starting an owner already stopped before spawning left startup unresolved.
System stdout/stderr errors escaped the failure boundary before fixed handlers were installed.

protocol.concurrency: one pending command, busy rejects without queue or sequence allocation
protocol.fatal_behavior: fixed Promise rejection, immediate owned child termination, one failed event, no retry
protocol.legacy: canonical ready without control_protocol can start but cannot use model control

boundaries: Tests use synthetic child processes, synthetic credentials and an in-memory synthetic encryption provider.
The root owns actual Python pipe integration and native Windows safeStorage acceptance.
No renderer, preload, main-process UI or Python source was changed by this assignment.
Package inclusion is owned by the root.
withSecret callback results are ignored; no claim is made that immutable JS strings can be reliably erased.
No real material, real key, external provider request, dependency installation or commit.
